summary: Favorites and alert subscriptions assigned to stale users after org migration
description:
Issue summary: After a customer-initiated org merge (org B merged into org A), several users in BrightRoute Labs report that their saved dashboard favorites and alert subscriptions were reassigned to user accounts that no longer exist in the org (stale user entries). The console still shows the favorite/alert metadata but the target user is unreachable and notifications are being dropped.

Observed behavior: Favorites & alert subscriptions list the old email/uid (pre-merge) in UI tooltips and in the API payloads. Attempts to edit or transfer ownership fail with 'user not found' errors. Some alerts are not firing because the subscription endpoint resolves to the stale user and fails delivery, but audit logs indicate the alert evaluation ran successfully.

Expected behavior: After org merge, favorites and alert subscriptions should be re-mapped to existing members when possible, or show a clear orphaned state in the UI and surface remediation steps. Alert notifications should fall back to org-level owners/teams rather than silently dropping when subscription targets are invalid.
impact: Multiple dashboard owners (5+ dashboards) and ~12 alert subscriptions are currently orphaned. Customer reports missed alert notifications for two production jobs overnight. Business impact: delayed on-call response and degraded trust in alerting. Workload: BrightRoute is an enterprise customer with SLA expectations.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Perform org merge: import/migrate users from source org (B) into destination org (A) using org-merge tool
2) Observe that pre-merge dashboard favorites and alert subscriptions retain original owner metadata in console UI and via GET /api/v1/alerts?org=
3) Attempt to reassign ownership via console -> Dashboard -> Share -> Transfer ownership, receive 'user not found' error
4) Review audit logs: alerts evaluated but delivery errors recorded with 'recipient id does not exist'
logs: Sample alert delivery error (prod-us-east, 2026-03-09T03:14:22Z): 'delivery.failure: recipient_not_found uid=usr-824283-premerge'. Console API GET /api/v1/favorites returned owner_id: usr-824283-premerge and owner_email: 'ingesta+old@brightroute.example'
investigation_notes:
Initial triage by Support: confirmed via API that favorites/alerts stored owner_id strings that were not in destination org's user table post-merge. Audit trail shows org-merge job wrote metadata without running identity reconciliation. Related internal ticket INT-7842 tracks an earlier migration job that had 'retain_original_ids' flag enabled. Hypothesis: org-merge process only copied references to original owner IDs and did not invoke post-merge canonicalization job.

Evidence: DB snapshot (prod-redwood-01) shows favorites.owner_id values pointing to deleted_user_ids table. Alert subscription delivery attempted to enqueue webhook to user-specific channel using owner_id; delivery service rejects unknown owner ids at enqueue time. Also observed retention compaction prune job has compacted some historical identity mappings; the canonicalization job relies on those mappings and is failing for oldest records.

Potential risk: If canonicalization job is re-run blindly it could overwrite live ownership metadata for dashboards that were intentionally transferred; need safe-merge plan.
comments: Support (Maya Thompson) 2026-03-09: Customer reports 12 stuck alert subscriptions and 5 dashboard favorites orphaned after org merge. Provided temporary workaround: export alert definitions and create org-level team subscriptions.
SRE (Ravi Patel) 2026-03-10: Confirmed owner_id references to deleted_user_ids. Created INT-7842 to track migration flag investigation. Will not run ad-hoc canonicalization without engineering plan.

Eng (Priya Nair) 2026-03-11: Hypothesis: org-merge retained 'external_id' instead of mapping to new internal uid. Proposed approach: run id-resolution job with dry-run to produce remap list. Need customer approval and backup snapshot. Blocking: retention compaction removed some legacy mapping rows (see compaction-window-2026-02).

Customer (Alex Reynolds, BrightRoute) 2026-03-12: We need alerts restored or re-routed to team channels ASAP. Willing to accept manual reassignments for impacted dashboards. Asked for ETA on canonicalization run.

Support (Maya Thompson) 2026-03-13: Scheduled a maintenance window with customer for 2026-03-15 02:00-03:00 UTC for a controlled id-resolution dry-run. Requested DB snapshot and acceptance of risk statement.

Eng (Ravi Patel) 2026-03-14: Dry-run completed in staging against a scrubbed export; remap suggested 12 owner_id -> uid mappings and 3 orphaned subscriptions requiring manual rebind. Preparing runbook and rollback plan.
resolution: In Progress: runbook drafted. Next steps: (1) take DB snapshot, (2) run id-resolution in prod during agreed maintenance window, (3) for any orphaned subscriptions, create org-level team bindings and notify customer. Post-action follow-ups: add org-merge canonicalization to pipeline and add pre-merge validation to prevent future writes with stale owner_ids. Customer has been offered a manual reassignment support pack free-of-charge.
next_steps: 1) Finalize rollback playbook and testing checklist. 2) Execute prod dry-run during 2026-03-15 window if customer approves. 3) Post-mortem and add a blocking validation to org-merge tool to fail when identity mapping cannot be resolved.
notes: Related to retention: older mapping rows were removed by retention compaction (policy retention=90 days) which contributed to inability to auto-resolve. Engineering to propose retention exception for identity-mapping table for 7 days around run.
